end.parentNote: Atharv practised looking closely at features such as beaks and feet, using words like “long,” “pointed,” and “webbed.” They connected webbed feet with swimming birds and explained that observations should focus on what is seen. They mixed up some feature descriptions and needed prompts; the later answers about webbed feet and a cone-shaped beak showed partial correction. At home, look at one bird or plant together and name two visible features, such as beak shape, feet, or leaf shape.
